context: Collapsible taxonomy tree with live search — a data visualization showing biological taxonomy (Life → Domain → Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family) with expand/collapse and keyword search.
first_impression: Clean and functional with thoughtful details, but the tree occupies only the top portion of the viewport leaving a large blank void below, and the typographic hierarchy is flat across all rank levels.
what_works: Deliberate use of the Paul Tol accessible palette instead of schemeCategory10 shows real color intentionality; the count badges (+37, +16) in monospace alongside the search icon embedded in the input are polished micro-details that elevate the UX above a first-draft chart.
what_doesnt: The bottom half of the viewport is entirely empty — the tree doesn't fill or center within the available space, making the layout feel unfinished; node labels are uniformly 12px with no weight or size variation across ranks, so Domain and Family nodes read identically, eliminating any typographic hierarchy.
